name: MyChannels
overview: Fork of JPKribs Live Channels with an expanded scheduling model and filler support.
description: MyChannels is a fork of JPKribs' Live Channels plugin, extended with per-entry weight and block size, weighted round-robin scheduling, filler pools for bumpers and trailers, an auto-generated Up Next card, and event-driven cache invalidation. Channels, their guide, and their streams are served in-process through Jellyfin's own Live TV.

versions.changelog: Add a diagnostic log line at every channel resolve, dumping the override table (id, weight, blockSize) and the resolved per-group scheduler input (id, series/title, weight, blockSize, item count). Lets a 'weight not respected' report be checked against actual scheduler input without needing to inspect the plugin config XML — a mismatch between the override id and the group's TopLevelItemId is the exact bug we're hunting.

Hotfix for v1.3.0.0 custom-bumper upload. ApiClient.ajax was serialising the File object as JSON and shipping mangled bytes to the server, which then failed the MP4 sniff and silently rejected the upload. Replace the upload call with a plain XMLHttpRequest carrying the file as its raw body and the Jellyfin auth token as X-Emby-Token, so the file's actual bytes reach the endpoint.

New FillerMode.CustomBumper. Upload an MP4 (H.264 + AAC) per channel that plays before every program at its own duration, bypassing auto-card generation entirely. Files live under the plugin cache dir (never in the config XML) with only a small flag + probed duration stashed on the channel. Channels with a custom bumper automatically use the per-item stream pipeline so an arbitrary bumper's resolution/framerate/audio properties don't have to match the main content the concat demuxer would otherwise require.

Fix race in Plugin.UpdateConfiguration: schedule cache was being cleared BEFORE the new config was persisted, so a concurrent tune-in or guide refresh firing in that window would rebuild the cache using the OLD in-memory config and immediately repopulate it. Symptom: turning FillerMode off on a channel had no effect until the next full RefreshGuide, because tune-ins kept serving the pre-save cache. Persist first, then clear.

SnapToBoundary cards use a truncation model: one card file per program at the max pad length (SnapMinutes), trimmed at stream time to the actual pad needed. Card set stays bounded (one per program) regardless of loop reshuffles or rotation shifts — no combinatorial explosion. Channels with FillerMode=SnapToBoundary automatically use the per-item stream pipeline (concat mode can't truncate).

Filler generation is now lazy and polite. AutoCardService.EnsureCard is a pure cache lookup; a separate Preheat schedules background generation. Each resolve preheats at most the first 3 missing cards, so channels with dozens of programs don't spawn dozens of ffmpegs. Successive RefreshGuide passes pick up more as needed, and cards for programs that never actually air never get generated. Background ffmpegs run at Idle priority (nice ~19 on Linux) with a concurrency of 1, so on shared hosting they never contend with a viewer's live-stream encoder.

Hotfix for v1.2.0.0: card generation moves fully off the tune-in critical path. A tune-in used to try to generate every missing card synchronously before the stream could start, blowing past ffmpeg timeouts and killing the whole session. Cards now generate in the background with a small concurrency cap; missing cards on a first tune-in are simply skipped, and they appear on the next resolve pass. Subsequent tune-ins with cached cards behave exactly as designed.

Filler subsystem: new per-channel Auto Up Next card setting. Off (default), FixedBumper (short card before every program), or SnapToBoundary (variable-length card that pads program-end to the next 15/30/60-minute grid so programs start on tidy times like broadcast TV). Cards show the next program's backdrop with an 'Up Next' overlay + a subtle Ken Burns zoom to fight burn-in during long slates. Cached to disk; generated once per (program, duration).

Content Weights UI: switch Weight and Block-size inputs from number spinners to dropdowns (0-10 weight, 1-6 block). Movie/music-video rows now show a disabled Block dropdown so they line up visually with series/collection rows instead of ragging short. Unknown stored values are added as extra options so nothing round-trips wrong.

Full-loop scheduling: each shuffled loop now airs every top-level item's blocks (shorter groups wrap and repeat when they run out). New Series interleave setting: Same keeps the group deal order stable across cycles (TNG, DS9, VOY every cycle); Shuffled reshuffles the order per cycle (TNG, DS9, VOY then DS9, VOY, TNG). Both deterministic — guide and stream agree.

Rework the Content Weights section to use the same jpk-collapsible-section pattern as every other folded section on the channels page. The v1.1.0.0 implementation used a different pattern that didn't wire up correctly against the shared collapsible handler.

Scheduling rewrite. Weight and Block-size are now set per top-level item in the channel (series, movie, collection) rather than as channel-wide FavorKind/EpisodesPerBlock knobs. Editor gains a Content Weights section that lists the resolved items with per-row inputs. FavorKind/FavorStrength/EpisodesPerBlock are deprecated (ignored by the scheduler and hidden from the UI; kept in the model for one release for XML round-trip). A warning is logged on plugin load for any channel that still carries a legacy FavorKind so you can set per-entry weights instead.

Roll back the save-flow visible-progress attempts from v1.0.0.3-1.0.0.5 — none produced visible feedback in the plugin-page context. Restored the upstream green-text-at-end pattern. Kept the two round-trip cuts (in-memory config on channels-tab save, cached RefreshGuide task id).

Replace the save-flow progress feedback with a self-contained top-right toast. The v1.0.0.4 window.Loading approach produced no visible feedback in the plugin page context. Zero dependency on Jellyfin globals now — Save, Import, Delete, etc. show a fixed-position spinner + text that can't be missed, and surface real error messages on failure.

Use Jellyfin's built-in Loading spinner overlay for the save-flow progress feedback. The v1.0.0.3 button-innerHTML approach was invisible in practice (the custom-element polyfill made the swap silently no-op); window.Loading.show/hide is the supported pattern every legacy Jellyfin controller uses.

Save-flow UX pass. Save, Import, Delete, Save Popular, Save Settings, and Rebuild Schedule now disable their trigger button, show a spinner, and surface real success/failure with the error message when things break — no more 5-10 seconds of silent frozen UI. Cached the RefreshGuide task id so save flows skip a task-enumeration round-trip. The channels tab now saves from its in-memory config instead of re-fetching first, cutting another round-trip (trade-off documented in the code: single-admin homelab only).

Fix hardcoded plugin GUID in the config-page JS. Under the fork's new GUID, /Plugins/{id}/Configuration was 404ing because the JS still asked for the upstream GUID; this aligns the JS with the plugin's actual identity.
Add MyChannels as a top-level dashboard sidebar entry (like Intro Skipper and Moonfin). One click from the sidebar instead of digging through Plugins.
Initial fork release. Includes the JS import subpath fix for reverse-proxy deployments; feature work per DESIGN.md follows in subsequent releases.
